angle: THERMAL, MASS, RELIABILITY and MANUFACTURING per watt of compute and per kg of Mercury: concentrated (A) vs film-distributed (B) vs hybrid (C)

assumptions.PV: thin c-Si, AM0 eta 0.20 at 301 K, -0.42 %/K, packing 0.90, alpha 0.90, eps_f 0.85, eps_b 0.90 (film) / 0.85 (wings); radiosity swarm model (thermal_result.json).
assumptions.energy_per_FLOP: 1.3e-13 J system-level dense FP8 at 85 C full clock x0.60 under-clocking = 7.8e-14 J at Tj 85 C; +0.89 %/K above 85 C (research_hotsi), -0.45 %/K below. A at Tj 105 C: 9.3e-14 J (+19.5 %%); B at Tj 85 C: 7.8e-14 J. Range low 4.1e-14 .. high 1.5e-13 J at 85 C. Same base for both: workload-matched (B neighbour-dataflow; A tightly coupled). For global/MoE/TP traffic on film, comm adds 10-99 %% energy (interconnect_final.json).
assumptions.delivered_satellite_kg_per_kg_rock: 0.50 (0.38-0.62): oxides reduced to Si/Mg/Al/Ca, O used as glass and EP propellant (17-37 %% overhead).
assumptions.Mercury: M 3.3011e23 kg; rock (crust+mantle) 8.05e22 kg = 24.4 %%; core 2.50e23 kg Fe-Ni-Si (Si 12.8 wt%%). Rock Si 1.87e22, Mg 1.61e22, Al 2.1e21, Na 1.05e21, K 3.5e19 kg.
assumptions.whole_planet_budget: rock x0.50 + core x0.65 (core Fe useful to A for pipes/structure/shielding; to B only its Si).
assumptions.meteoroids: Grun 1985 flux (SPENVIS), 20 km/s at 1 AU, flux ~r^-1.8 and speed ~r^-0.5 inside 1 AU; SPENVIS thin-plate BLE (K1 0.57) and Christiansen Whipple BLE.
assumptions.lifetime: 10 yr design life; attrition spares included in mass (B overbuild 5/10/20 %%, A radiator spares + A/B loops + PV reserve).

table.architecture: A concentrated (1 MW sats, HBM, Tj 105 C, NaK loops + SO2 heat-pipe blades)
table.element_limited_note: Rock-mass limit 5.8e37 FLOP/s is NOT reachable with NaK cooling: Mercury K (3.5e19 kg) caps NaK-78 loops at 1.4e+23 W of chips (1.5e+36 FLOP/s, f~0.3 %); Na-rich NaK 3.8e+23 W; Al-finned radiators cap at 1e+24 W unless Mg replaces Al. K-free options: SO2 pumped two-phase loops or pure-Na loops at >=105 C (Tj >= ~130 C, energy/op x1.5).
table.failure_blast_radius: Pumped-loop trunk hit drains one of two loops -> 0.5 MW (half a 1 MW satellite) throttled; both loops or module -> 1 MW. P(lose >=1 loop per satellite per decade) ~11 %; plus ~2.0 %/yr capacity from branch and heat-pipe hits (covered by spares). HV strings (300-1000 V) see ~5.8e+05 cell perforations/yr per MW, each a possible impact-plasma arc trigger (sustained arcs >=80-183 V).

table.architecture: B film-distributed (0.15 W chiplets at 2.5 cm, Tj 85 C, film = radiator)
table.element_limited_note: Rock-only Si (1.87e22 kg at 0.0995 kg Si/m2) builds 1.88e+23 m2 of film -> f=0.56 at 1.09 AU, 4.49e+38 FLOP/s (vs bulk-mass limit 4.7e+38); full shell needs core Si (whole planet: 5.1e+23 m2 vs 5.11e+23 needed).
table.failure_blast_radius: One chiplet + its PV cell: 0.10-0.25 W (4-11 cm2). Expected attrition 0.13 %/yr mid (0.019-1.22 %/yr) at 0.92 AU; no fluids, no HV (cell-level 0.5-1 V); latch-up current is limited by the chip's own cell.

table.architecture: C hybrid: B film + 10 % compute in A-type pods (switch/gateway + coupled shards)
table.failure_blast_radius: Film part as B (0.15 W); pods 0.1-0.3 MW each (as A).

clustering_penalty.note: Solid spreader mass per W grows linearly with chip power (P/(q_e k dT)); a heat-pipe vascular network costs a constant ~1/(2 w q_e) metres of pipe per W because the film between pipes cannot spread heat more than ~1.5-2 cm.

C1_heatpipe_tiles.verdict: The film cannot spread heat beyond ~1.5-2 cm, so tiles need a heat pipe every ~3 cm (~20-35 m of pipe per m2): 0.1-0.6 g/W (no lighter than Mg spreading for 0.15 W chiplets) and thin pipes are perforated at 1-10 %/yr. Rejected.

C2_radiator_film.verdict: No pumps or NaK; radiator film carries chiplets at ~1.4 kW/m2. ~1.5-2x the film (B) per W because the PV wing, HV bus and conversion are still needed, and c-Si gains little from running hot. Dominated by B on mass and sunlight; useful only where radiator orientation must be controlled (e.g. to aim IR away from Earth).

element_limits.note_O: Half of rock O assumed available for glass; the rest is EP propellant (17-37 % of delivered mass).

blast_radius.heat_pipe_hit: one heat pipe = 0.25 m2 of panel

radiation.event: Aug-1972-class SEP (>10 MeV 1.96e10, >30 MeV 8.42e9 cm^-2; SWSC 2014 table)

tolerance.FinFET16_logic_rad: ~1e8 (100 Mrad: variability rises; to 1 Grad with degradation; Bonaldo/Ma et al.)
tolerance.HBM_rad: 2e3 (Suncatcher: HBM irregularities from 2 krad, no hard fails to 15 krad)

radiation.note: Order-of-magnitude only: single power-law spectra, approximate stopping power and range fits; 10-yr design assumed ~3-10 such event-equivalents. r^-2.5 radial scaling assumed.

yield.module_note: A module = 47 wafers + 2 NaK loops (~150 m2 armoured pipe, ~28 valves, 4 pumps) + ~5000 sealed SO2 heat pipes per MW; one leak or a failed weld scraps or reworks the loop; wafer-scale dies need on-wafer spare cores (Cerebras-style).

verdict: On thermal, mass, reliability and manufacturing grounds the film-distributed design (B) wins by ~8x in kg per watt (0.89 vs 7.2 g/W mid; even B-high 2.0 < A-low 4.4), ~10x in FLOP/s per kg of Mercury, ~1.7x in FLOP/s per W of sunlight, and by 6-7 orders of magnitude in failure blast radius (0.15 W vs 0.5-1 MW). Concentration buys no PV advantage: at its mass optimum the concentrated wing sits at 0.86 AU and 347 K, the same temperature as the film; running wings hot at 0.6 AU costs +9 % mass and -40 % sunlight use. The concentrated design pays a ~3.7 g/W "heat-transport tax" (MMOD-armoured NaK manifolds 1.2 g/W + heat-pipe radiator 2.3 g/W) that the film does not have (its Mg spreader is 0.11 g/W), and NaK-78 cooling is capped by Mercury's potassium at ~1.4e23 W of chips (0.04 % of L), below even an Earth-safe swarm. Best hybrid from this angle: C = film for the bulk of the compute plus a few % (3-10 %) of power in concentrated, shielded, pumped pods for switching, gateways and the tightly coupled shards that the interconnect study says the film cannot do; it costs 1.1-1.5 g/W. Use pure concentrated modules (A or wafer-scale-SRAM A') only where coupling demands it, and cool them with SO2 heat-pipe blades fed by Na-rich or K-free loops.

findings.headline: Mass per watt of compute: film 0.89 g/W (0.47-1.98) vs concentrated 7.2 g/W (4.4-15.1); 8-9x at equal junction temperature too
findings.detail: B at 0.92 AU, f=0.01: c-Si 30 um 0.36 g/W, glass cover+emitters 0.32, Mg spreader (13 um for 0.15 W chiplets, dT 10 K) 0.11, structure 0.06, grid 0.02, lasers 0.02, chiplets 0.002; areal 0.17 kg/m2 (inside the 0.06-0.2 target). A at 0.86 AU, 1 MW satellites: radiator (SO2/Al heat-pipe blades sized for <=1 %/yr MMOD loss, 1.8 kg/m2, 1.3 m2/kW) 2.3 g/W, compute module 1.5, NaK loops 1.2, PV wing 1.0, shielding 0.3, conversion 0.3, lasers/attitude/booms 0.3, bus 0.07, fixed 0.15. Equal-Tj check: Tj 85 C 7.85 vs 0.89 g/W; Tj 105 C 7.18 vs 0.79 g/W.

findings.headline: Concentrated wings do not want to run hot: mass optimum is 0.86 AU (flat 0.7-1.0 AU) at 347 K, not 0.6 AU at 422 K
findings.detail: c-Si yield peaks at 0.6 AU (332 W/m2) but the wing is only ~1 g/W of 7.2; meteoroid flux (~r^-1.8) thickens radiator/loop armour inward. At 0.6 AU: 7.81 g/W and 0.070 W of chip power per W of sunlight intercepted, vs 7.19 g/W and 0.116-0.122 at 0.86-0.9 AU. Under a sunlight limit, hot PV wastes 40 % of the light.

findings.headline: Heat transport is the concentrated design's structural tax: coolant inventory ~ path length/(c_p dT v)
findings.detail: Branched NaK manifolds over 4 square blades, optimised dT_loop 40 K and 6 m/s: 0.33 kg NaK/kW, pump power 3.3 % (EM pump eta 0.25; 15-18 % if eta 0.05 as in NASA FSP ALIP tests), loops 1.2 g/W with A/B redundancy. Satellite optimum ~0.3-1 MW (7.6 g/W); 10 MW 9.8, 100 MW 19.2 g/W: km-scale wings need 830 m Al buses at 20 % I2R loss (1.25 g/W) and 2.3 kg/kW of NaK.

findings.headline: Film lateral spreading forbids clustering: spreader mass per W grows linearly with chip power
findings.detail: Minimum-mass tapered spreader M = rho pi P^2/(16 q_e k dT): Mg 0.09 g/W at 0.1 W, 0.94 g/W at 1 W, 9.4 g/W at 10 W. Uniform Mg: 0.15 W -> 13 um; 0.25 W -> 40 um (0.30 g/W); 1 W -> 248 um (1.9 g/W). Heat-pipe "tiles" need a pipe every ~3 cm (36 m of pipe per m2, 0.16-0.63 g/W) and thin pipes lose 1-21 %/yr to meteoroids. Clustered tiles are rejected.

findings.headline: Mercury potassium caps NaK-cooled concentrated compute below an Earth-safe swarm
findings.detail: Rock K ~3.5e19 kg (surface 1288 ppm GRS, mantle K2O 0.045 wt%). NaK-78 at 0.33 kg/kW -> 1.4e23 W of chips (1.5e36 FLOP/s, f~0.3 %); Na-rich NaK (~28 wt% K, liquidus estimated 40-60 C) 3.8e23 W. Al-finned radiators cap at 1e24 W (Al 2.1e21 kg) unless Mg replaces Al. K-free cooling: SO2 pumped two-phase (S and O are abundant), or pure Na loops >=105 C (Tj >=130 C, E/op x1.5). The film needs no K or Al beyond grid lines; it is Si-limited (rock Si builds 1.9e23 m2 = f 0.56).

findings.headline: SO2 is a Mercury-native heat-pipe fluid for 330-370 K; ammonia/water are not (no hydrogen)
findings.detail: NIST properties: SO2 merit number 2.2e10 W/m2 at 356 K (0.46x ammonia, 0.05x water), 1.9 MPa. NH3 inventory for 1e25 W of radiators would need ~1e19 kg of H vs ~1e13 kg in Mercury's polar ice.

findings.headline: Swarm totals: film reaches ~4.5e38 FLOP/s from Mercury's rock and the sunlight limit 8e38 with the whole planet; concentrated 5.8e37 (bulk) but 1.5e36 (K-limited)
findings.detail: Mass-limited coverage: B f=0.56-0.59 (Si/mass) at ~1.1 AU; A f=0.12 at 0.92 AU. Sunlight-limited (f=1): B 8.0e38 FLOP/s at 1.35 AU needing 0.31 Mercury masses (core Si needed); A 5.7e38 at 1.59 AU needing 1.6 Mercury masses (impossible). FLOP/s per kg of Mercury rock: B 8.7e15, C 5.0e15, A' 9.5e14, A 7.5e14. FLOP/s per W of sunlight: B 2.1e12, A 1.25e12 (f=0.01).

findings.headline: Blast radius: film 0.10-0.25 W per failure, ~0.13 %/yr attrition; concentrated 0.5-1 MW per loop/module failure, ~11 % chance per satellite-decade
findings.detail: Grun flux at 0.92 AU: 110 /m2/yr perforate (>=1e-9 g), 1.7 /m2/yr >=1e-6 g. Film loses a 0.15 W cell when hit by >=1e-6 g (0.11 %/yr; 0.007-1.2 %/yr for 1e-5..1e-7 g kill thresholds) plus 0.02 %/yr direct die hits. A: Whipple-armoured trunks still give 0.006 loop drains/yr per loop, branches 1 %/yr and heat pipes 0.5 %/yr of radiator; 1 MW of HV wing sees 5.8e5 cell perforations/yr, each a potential impact-plasma arc trigger (sustained arcs above 80-183 V in light-gas-gun tests). Film cells run at 0.5-1 V and latch-up is limited by each chip's own cell.

findings.headline: Radiation: unshielded film chiplets take ~0.1-1 Mrad per decade even with a 0.1-0.5 mm glass die cap; fine for FinFET/SOI logic+SRAM, fatal for DRAM/HBM
findings.detail: Aug-1972-class event (>10 MeV 2e10 cm^-2): bare back side 0.27-2.4 Mrad, through the 30 um Si + 20 um glass front 40-140 krad, with 0.5 mm glass cap 5.5 krad; a module behind 5 g/cm2 of Mercury rock ~0.2 krad. 16 nm bulk FinFETs tolerate ~100 Mrad; HBM shows errors from ~2 krad. So film memory must be SRAM/MRAM; HBM-class memory only in shielded modules.

findings.headline: Manufacturing: same PV area and die area per MW; the film adds 6.7e6 chiplet placements/MW, the module adds ~5,300 sealed heat pipes, 150 m2 of armoured NaK pipe, 28 valves and 4 pumps per MW
findings.detail: PV 4,620 (B) vs 4,660 (A) m2/MW; 47 x 300 mm wafers/MW at 0.3 W/mm2 either way. Film tolerates dead chiplets (die yield 99.93 % at 0.75 mm2, bond yield 99-99.99 %, no rework); modules need leak-tight welds and on-wafer redundancy (reticle die yield 45 %). Under Mercury's surface heat cap (4.1e18 W, 13.5 MJ/kg) the film adds 1.1e22 W/yr of compute vs 1.3e21 for modules (1e24 W in 93 vs 750 yr), needing 2.3e15 chiplet placements/s.

findings.headline: Earth: both sit just inside Earth's orbit; the film must stay below f~0.25 (Tj 85 C) to avoid crossing 0.983 AU; any f above ~0.5 % forces Earth by >1 W/m2
findings.detail: Mass-optimal: A 0.86-0.91 AU, B 0.92-0.94 AU (f 0.01-0.1). Forcing per unit coverage 179 W/m2 (A at 0.86 AU), 213 (B at 0.92 AU); 1 % coverage = 1.8-2.1 W/m2 (0.5-0.6x CO2 doubling); 10 % = 21-23 W/m2. Film placement reaches Earth perihelion at f=0.25 (Tj 85 C), 0.58 (105 C), 0.82 (125 C); the rock-mass-limited film (f~0.56, 1.1 AU) encloses Earth (~400 W/m2). Earth-safe cap (1 W/m2): f<=0.5 %, ~2.5e23 W, ~3.4e36 FLOP/s, needing 2e20 kg (film) or 1.8e21 kg (modules), and A cannot reach even that with NaK-78.

open_questions: Na-K liquidus on the Na-rich side (ideal-solution estimate used): sets how much K a concentrated swarm needs.
SO2 heat pipes and pumped two-phase SO2 loops are untested at scale (merit computed from NIST properties only); Mg/Al compatibility with dry SO2 over 10 yr.

Cell-kill threshold for meteoroid hits on free-standing 20-50 um c-Si film (crack propagation, shunting): drives film attrition 0.007-1.2 %/yr; a monolithic brittle film under spin tension may need segmenting into tiles on a Mg mesh.
Impact-plasma arc probability per perforation on 300-1000 V strings in solar-wind plasma (no data found for interplanetary densities).
Solar-proton dose: order-of-magnitude only (single power-law spectra, approximate stopping powers); needs SHIELDOSE/ESP runs at 0.9 AU.
Workload mix: the film's FLOP/s assume neighbour-dataflow work (comm +3 %); global/MoE/TP traffic on film costs 10-99 % extra energy (interconnect_final).
High-throughput chiplet placement (2e15/s at the heat-cap build rate) on c-Si film without polymers (Al-Al thermocompression or direct bonding).
